newsitem.title: INDIA: TEXT-India raises FII equity limit.
newsitem.headline: TEXT-India raises FII equity limit.

text.p: Following is the text of a statement by the Indian government announcing an increase in the limit on foreign institutional investment in equity capital to 30 percent from 24 percent.
"The government has notified enhancement of limits on investments by foreign institutional investors (FIIs) from 24 percent to 30 percent.
It may be recalled that the Finance Minister P. Chidambaram in his budget speech on February 28, 1997 had announced an increase in FIIs' investment ceiling.

Under the new guidelines, companies would be permitted to raise the aggregate portfolio investment limits by all FIIs, non-resident Indians (NRIs) and overseas commercial bodies (OCBs) up to 30 percent of the issued and paid up capital of a company subject to:
(a) Approval by the board of directors of the company to the enhanced limit up to 30 percent; and
(b) A special resolution passed by the general body of the company approving the enhanced limit up to 30 percent.
The present investment limits for an individual FII, NRI or OCB would remain unaltered."
